subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots continue inheriting all host security overrides, or should OpenClaw filter or scope overrides such as `path-to-regexp` when they conflict with a plugin's own dependency graph?
rationale: The source-level conflict is clear, but the permanent boundary is a maintainer policy choice because security override propagation protects OpenClaw installs while this specific override breaks valid Express 4.x plugin packages.

options.title: Scope Managed Overrides
options.body: Filter or namespace host overrides for managed plugin roots so core security pins do not override plugin-owned dependency contracts when the plugin graph requires a different major version.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep current override propagation and add Express 4/path-to-regexp validation that tells plugin authors to add a package-local override or migrate to Express 5.

options.title: Keep Current Policy
options.body: Treat this as plugin package ownership and require affected plugins such as camofox-browser to ship their own override or migrate off Express 4.

recommendation.title: Scope Managed Overrides
recommendation.body: Filter or namespace host overrides for managed plugin roots so core security pins do not override plugin-owned dependency contracts when the plugin graph requires a different major version.

likelyOwner.reason: The current managed npm override propagation and workspace override evidence both point to this person as the clearest code-history owner for the policy decision.
